title: In repos/development-vessel/src/vacuous-edit.ts, the reference-counting view deletes most of the file before counting, s
description:
In repos/development-vessel/src/vacuous-edit.ts, the reference-counting view deletes most of the file before counting, so used bindings read as unused. Make two changes.

CHANGE 1 — append this function at the very end of the file, after the last line:

/**
 * A "code only" view for reference counting: comment lines dropped, string
 * literals blanked ONE LINE AT A TIME.
 *
 * The previous form chained three whole-file regex replaces. An apostrophe in a
 * prose comment is not a string delimiter, but the first replace treats it as one
 * and pairs it with the next apostrophe anywhere later in the file. Measured on
 * goal-host-vessel/src/index.ts: 1,048,462 characters became 519,801 after the
 * apostrophe pass, then 279,328 after the quote pass had run across the now
 * unbalanced remainder — 73.4 percent of the file deleted, taking all six
 * references to the binding `uf` with it. The gate then reported `uf` as never
 * used and refused a correct repair.
 *
 * Line scoping means a stray apostrophe can corrupt at most its own line.
 */
export function codeOnlyView(source: string): string {
  return source
    .split("\n")
    .filter((l) => !/^\s*(?:\/\/|\*|\/\*)/.test(l))
    .map((l) => l
      .replace(/'(?:[^'\\]|\\.)*'/g, "''")
      .replace(/"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"/g, '""')
      .replace(/`(?:[^`\\]|\\.)*`/g, "``"))
    .join("\n");
}

CHANGE 2 — replace these exact four lines:
  const codeOnly = after
    .replace(/'(?:[^'\\]|\\.)*'/g, "''")
    .replace(/"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"/g, '""')
    .replace(/`(?:[^`\\]|\\.)*`/g, "``");

with this exact single line:
  const codeOnly = codeOnlyView(after);

Nothing else changes. Verified against the real file before dispatching: after this change the binding `uf` counts 5 references so the gate stops refusing, and the case the stripping was originally written for still works — a name bound and then used only inside a string literal still counts 1 reference and is still correctly reported unused.
